description: The fatal READ arm of 1000-ACCTFILE-GET-NEXT at app/cbl/CBACT01C.cbl:L92-L116, and the read-site counterpart of case10's fatal OPEN arm: the two share the three-line abend tail and differ in the second line, which is the literal belonging to the paragraph that failed. What the case declares: one ACCTFILE row, so the dataset is there and 0000-ACCTFILE-OPEN succeeds at L136 with '00' - this case is about the READ and not the OPEN - and the very first READ at L93 then reports a permanent error, because the stored row is not a CVACT01Y record. It measures 122 bytes where app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy declares 300, and 122 is not an arbitrary number: it is the sum of the twelve named spans (11 + 1 + 12 + 12 + 12 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 12 + 12 + 10 + 10), which is the account record with its trailing FILLER PIC X(178) span absent, 300 - 178. From ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS onward the bytes are the first row of app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt verbatim, including the three '{' zoned sign overpunches that close the S9(10)V99 spans at offsets 13, 25 and 37; only ACCT-ID is changed, to 00000000601, an identifier no row of that fixture carries, so this row can never be mistaken for one of the fifty stored records. On the choice of input, stated so the intent is explicit: rows are DECLARED and none of them is ever reached, rather than an empty row list. An empty list is not expressible here - DatasetInput admits exactly one of "rows", "fixture" or "empty": true, and an empty list declares none of the three - and "empty": true would be the wrong assertion in any event: it describes a dataset that exists and holds no row, whose first READ reports '10' and ends the loop cleanly, which is case02 and the opposite arm to this one. The ladder at L94-L103 is evaluated in source order and only its third arm is taken. L94 IF ACCTFILE-STATUS = '00' would MOVE 0 TO APPL-RESULT and PERFORM 1100-DISPLAY-ACCT-RECORD: not taken. L98 ELSE IF ACCTFILE-STATUS = '10' would MOVE 16 TO APPL-RESULT, which satisfies the 88 APPL-EOF condition declared at L63 and ends the loop silently through L108's MOVE 'Y' TO END-OF-FILE: not taken, because the status reported is not '10'. L100-L101 ELSE MOVE 12 TO APPL-RESULT: taken. The guard chain then fails twice - 88 APPL-AOK at L104 is false because APPL-RESULT is 12 and not 0, and 88 APPL-EOF at L107 is false because it is 12 and not 16 - so L109-L113 run in order: DISPLAY 'ERROR READING ACCOUNT FILE' at L110, MOVE ACCTFILE-STATUS TO IO-STATUS at L111, PERFORM 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS at L112 which emits the status line, and PERFORM 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM at L113 which displays 'ABENDING PROGRAM' at L170, moves 0 into TIMING at L171 and 999 into ABCODE at L172, and calls 'CEE3ABD' at L173. This is precisely the branch a translation that treated any non-'00' status as end of data would get wrong: it would move 16 instead of 12, set END-OF-FILE, close the file and reach the closing banner with return code 0, silently converting a permanent I/O error into a clean end of file. The return code here is therefore 12, from the MOVE 12 at L101 and carried out by the CALL 'CEE3ABD'; it is never 16, which is the APPL-EOF value, never 0, and never 999 - ABCODE 999 at L172 and TIMING 0 at L171 are Language Environment abend parameters and are not the return code. The second line is 26 characters and contains the word ACCOUNT. The program's three error literals are deliberately inconsistent and are reproduced exactly as they are rather than harmonised: the read literal at L110 is 'ERROR READING ACCOUNT FILE' at 26 characters, the open literal at L144 is the bare DD name in 'ERROR OPENING ACCTFILE' at 22, and the close literal at L162 is 'ERROR CLOSING ACCOUNT FILE' at 26. case10 states the open literal; this case states the read one, and the difference between the two second lines is the point of having both. Deriving the status line, step by step from the renderer: 01 IO-STATUS-04 is IO-STATUS-0401 PIC 9 followed by IO-STATUS-0403 PIC 999 at L57-L59, four bytes in total, and both arms of 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS display the 20-character literal 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by that image, so the line is 24 characters and the NNNN is part of the hard-coded literal at L183 and L187 rather than a placeholder awaiting substitution. The numeric ELSE arm at L184-L187 is taken when IO-STATUS is numeric and IO-STAT1 is not '9': MOVE '0000' TO IO-STATUS-04, then MOVE IO-STATUS TO IO-STATUS-04(3:2), which overlays the third and fourth bytes only. A z/OS permanent I/O error reports FILE STATUS '30', whose first byte '3' is not '9' and which is numeric, so it takes that arm and renders 0, 0, 3, 0 - FILE STATUS IS: NNNN0030. The IF arm at L177-L183 is taken instead when IO-STATUS is not numeric or IO-STAT1 is '9': it moves IO-STAT1 into IO-STATUS-04(1:1) and the binary value of IO-STAT2 into IO-STATUS-0403. This translation reaches its data through a configuration-bound JDBC driver whose refusal carries no VSAM feedback code to report, so AccountRepository reports PERMANENT_ERROR_STATUS - '9' followed by a binary-zero feedback byte - for a row whose width it will not decode fields from, and that status takes the IF arm, renders 9 then 000, and gives FILE STATUS IS: NNNN9000, also 24 characters. The frozen contract fixes that value rather than leaving it to a case: FileStatus declares no '30' at all, and CBACT01CParityTest requires every case whose return code is not zero to end with the rendering composed from AccountRepository.PERMANENT_ERROR_STATUS followed by 'ABENDING PROGRAM'. This case therefore states 9000, and the divergence from the mainframe's 0030 is recorded here rather than silently resolved - the same treatment case10 gives the open arm's 0035. What the branch it pins does not depend on is the four-character image: the arm reached, the literal displayed, the guard chain that fails twice and the return code 12 are all identical either way. Nothing is displayed before the failure: the first READ never yielded a decodable record, so no labelled field line, no 49-dash separator and no 300-byte record image appears anywhere in SYSOUT. Nothing is displayed after it either, because L173 terminates the program - 9000-ACCTFILE-CLOSE at L83 is never performed, so no 'ERROR CLOSING ACCOUNT FILE' line can appear, and the closing banner at L85 is never reached. SYSOUT is exactly these four lines, of 38, 26, 24 and 16 characters. Nothing is written anywhere, and "expectedWrites" being empty asserts that positively rather than expressing a lack of interest. No final state is reported for ACCTFILE and none is expected: a 122-byte row has no 300-byte layout to be described by, and describing it under one would be a false statement about its bytes rather than an assertion about them. case14 pins this same arm from the other direction with a row one byte too wide at 301, which a decoder that read the first 300 bytes and ignored the rest would pass while failing this one. The case is deterministic: the condition it forces is a fixed literal row width, and it carries no wall-clock value and no random value. It declares no job parameter, because app/jcl/READACCT.jcl:L22 is a bare EXEC PGM=CBACT01C with no PARM. The dataset is addressed only by its binding key, ACCTFILE, which is the DD name at app/jcl/READACCT.jcl:L25; no fully-qualified dataset name appears here, because those live only in application.yml. Every line and every byte of the seeded row is US-ASCII, the code page of app/data/ASCII and of ParityHarness.FIXTURE_CHARSET, and never a platform default. Provenance: statically derived by reading app/cbl/CBACT01C.cbl, app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy, app/jcl/READACCT.jcl and app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt, cross-checked against the constants published by AccountBalanceJob, AbendException, AccountRepository and FileStatus. Nothing here was captured from a run of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment - there is no z/OS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler as disabled, and no Language Environment CEE service exists to link the CALL 'CEE3ABD' at L173 - and that substitution of provenance, and nothing else about the gate, is the escalated deviation recorded as risk R-A.
